material_systems.name: Solvent-Based MDF Edge Sealer

primer.notes: MUST be applied to MDF cut/routed edges BEFORE any latex product. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber swelling on MDF edges. Step 1 of two-step MDF prime. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine SS2.1 and SS4.1. Built-in carcass has extensive cut edges at shelf dado joints, face frame rabbets, and routed profiles.

material_systems.notes: Edge-only application. Step 1 of MDF two-step prime process. Built-in openings have high edge density — multiple shelves, dividers, and back panel rabbets per opening.

material_systems.name: High-Build Latex Face Primer for MDF

primer.notes: Applied to MDF face surfaces AFTER edge sealing with shellac/oil-based. Builds film, levels surface. Step 2 of two-step MDF prime. Built-in shelf faces, side panels, and back panels are typically MDF face surfaces.

material_systems.notes: Step 2 of MDF two-step prime. Face surfaces only — edges already sealed.

material_systems.name: Stain-Blocking Primer for FJP/Poplar

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Oil-Based Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY for bare FJP. Resin and green mineral streaks bleed through standard latex primers without stain-blocking. NOT optional. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine SS2.2 and SS4.1.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Stain-blocking is not optional for FJP built-in components.

material_systems.name: Tannin-Blocking Primer for Hardwood

primer.notes: Blocks tannin bleed-through on bare hardwood (oak, cherry, walnut, maple). Per Millwork Doctrine SS4.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Required for all bare hardwood built-in substrates.

primer.notes: Standard primer-sealer for bare softwood built-in components. Seals and provides tooth for finish coat.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel

products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
finish.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Built-in interiors benefit from fast dry for efficient multi-coat workflow — compartments retain moisture longer than open surfaces. Same system as trim, window, riser, wainscot, wood wall, and arch element specs.

material_systems.notes: QT3 — satin is the only sheen per sheen/QT gate (FFD SS4.1). Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel

products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
finish.notes: Superior flow and leveling — critical for built-in shelf faces where brush marks are visible. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away (FFD SS15.3.1). Deep compartments amplify dry time concerns — enclosed spaces retain humidity. Same system as trim, window, riser, wainscot, wood wall, and arch element specs.

material_systems.notes: QT4. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel

finish.coat_notes: QT5 brush typically requires 3+ coats per FFD SS15.10.3.
finish.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Same system as trim, window, riser, wainscot, wood wall, and arch element specs.

material_systems.notes: QT5. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

coverage_profiles.notes: Built-in opening primer coverage. EA-based per opening tier using SF-equivalent conversion from BuiltIns Quantification System v2.0 (S~2SF, M~5SF, L~10SF, XL~20SF). These are material planning estimates for coverage calculation — production rates use EA/hr directly. MDF edges may absorb more sealer. Door/drawer fronts estimated at ~6 SF each (average front face only — painted flat).
assumptions: Single coat primer system (except MDF two-step: edge seal + face prime)
Opening counts from PaintScope inputs PS_OPENING_EA.BUILTIN_SHELF.*
SF equivalents are averages across typical residential built-in sizes

coverage_profiles.notes: Built-in opening finish coat coverage on primed smooth surface. Two-coat standard; third coat at QT5 brush has same per-coat coverage. Deep openings consume more material due to increased interior surface area — DEPTH modifier affects production time but not material coverage rate (rate stays same, just more surface area to cover). Door/drawer fronts estimated at ~6 SF each (front face + edges). Spray method: add 20-30% waste for overspray inside compartments.
assumptions: Deep openings have more interior surface area — material quantity scales with depth
Spray overspray waste higher inside enclosed compartments than open surfaces

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.usage: Floor protection at base of built-in work area and sawhorse zone for door painting
consumables.notes: Runner-style for built-in base perimeter. Additional coverage for sawhorse area when painting removed doors/drawers. Always required regardless of application method.

consumables.name: Masking tape (1.5" blue painter's tape)
consumables.usage: Wall masking at built-in-to-wall junction (spray only), edge masking for brush work on adjacent finished surfaces
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. Wall masking required for spray application method at built-in-to-wall junction. Brush application may need edge masking where built-in meets finished adjacent surfaces.

consumables.name: Masking paper (12-inch)
consumables.usage: Wall surface masking at built-in-to-wall junction (spray only)
consumables.notes: Paper + tape system for wall protection at built-in-to-wall junction during spray application. 12-inch width adequate for overspray drift from built-in spray work.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 180-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer sanding for bare substrates, factory primer scuff, initial surface prep
consumables.notes: 180 grit for initial bare wood sanding and factory primer scuff. Hand sanding or pad sanding. Built-in interiors require reaching into compartments — flexible sanding sponge acceptable for inside corners.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer final sand, between-coat sanding (QT3 spot, QT4 full)
consumables.notes: 220 grit for final prep sand and between-coat sanding. Rigid sanding block mandatory for flat shelf faces and face frames (FFD SS15.4.1). Flexible sanding sponge for inside corners and tight compartments.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.notes: 220-320 grit range at QT5. Uniform scratch pattern required. Built-in shelves, dividers, and door/drawer fronts all sanded to QT5 standard.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.usage: Rigid block for between-coat sanding. Mandatory per FFD SS15.4.1.
consumables.notes: One block per crew, reusable. Rigid block critical for flat shelf faces, side panels, and door/drawer fronts to avoid creating waves. Deep compartments may require smaller sanding blocks for access.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5")
consumables.usage: Primary brush for built-in interiors, face frames, and door/drawer fronts
consumables.notes: 2-2.5 inch for compartment interiors, shelf faces, and detail work. One per painter per material change. Angled tip reaches into corners and dado joints.

consumables.name: Mini foam roller (4-inch)
consumables.usage: Flat surfaces inside built-in compartments — shelf faces, back panels, side panels
consumables.notes: Foam mini roller for flat built-in surfaces. Provides smoother finish than brush on flat shelf faces. Used in combination with angled sash brush (brush for edges/corners, roller for field). One per painter per material change.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411
consumables.usage: Fine atomization for built-in compartment spray finish
consumables.notes: Tight fan pattern for built-in work. Spray reaches all interior surfaces uniformly — critical for deep compartments where brush access is difficult. Overspray inside enclosed compartments requires careful technique to avoid buildup.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.usage: Remove sanding dust before each coat application
consumables.notes: One tack cloth covers ~30 SF of built-in surface. Use before every coat. Built-in interiors trap sanding dust in corners and dado joints — thorough tack cloth pass required inside compartments.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.usage: Built-in-to-wall junctions, shelf-to-side panel joints, face frame-to-carcass joints
consumables.notes: Caulk at built-in-to-wall perimeter junction (~72 LF/tube NC rate per research). Interior caulk at visible shelf-to-side joints and face frame joints where gaps show. Higher caulk consumption than closet shelf due to visible finish quality requirements.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackle compound
consumables.usage: Fill fastener holes on built-in shelves, side panels, face frames
consumables.notes: ELEVATED CONSUMPTION in NC. Overfill-sand-flush method for fastener holes with HIGH waste factor per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine. Built-ins have high fastener density — shelves, dividers, face frames, and back panels all nailed/screwed. 3-5x standard spackle consumption per Millwork Doctrine.

consumables.name: Sandable wood filler
consumables.usage: Fill deeper defects, damaged edges, and knot holes on built-in components
consumables.notes: Lightweight or auto-body type depending on defect depth. Supplement to spackle for deeper fills. One quart per ~100 SF of built-in assembly.

floor_perimeter.description: Drop cloth runners at base of built-in work area
floor_perimeter.condition: application_method = brush — drip and sanding dust protection at built-in base. Standard for brush millwork.

floor_workzone.description: Localized floor coverage around spray target and sawhorse door painting area
floor_workzone.condition: application_method = spray — upgrades from floor_perimeter. Covers built-in spray zone plus sawhorse area for door/drawer front painting. Built-ins are discrete elements — not full room coverage.

wall_adjacent.description: Wall masking at built-in-to-wall junction to prevent overspray
wall_adjacent.condition: application_method = spray — paper + tape masking on wall surface adjacent to built-in. Required on sides and top where built-in meets finished wall.

fixture_covers.description: Ceiling fixture protection near spray work area
fixture_covers.condition: application_method = spray AND ceiling fixtures near work area — plastic bag or film covers.

required_inputs.purpose: Count of solid doors + drawer fronts to remove/paint/reinstall
Hardware piece count for removal/reinstall labor
Height classification for tall built-in modifier (floor-to-ceiling units)
Floor protection area at built-in base (brush)
Localized floor protection for spray + sawhorse area

compatibility_rules.description: All finish systems are compatible with all primer systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Primer and finish are independent selections. All combinations valid.

compatibility_rules.description: SS_PRIMED_FACTORY compatible with all finish systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Scuff sand factory primer for adhesion. No additional primer needed.

compatibility_rules.description: MDF two-step prime: shellac edge seal MUST precede latex face prime
compatibility_rules.notes: SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC on edges first, then SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX on faces. Never reverse. Water-based products on raw MDF edges cause irreversible fiber swelling.

compatibility_rules.description: Door/drawer fronts use same material systems as carcass openings
compatibility_rules.notes: Doors/drawers removed from built-in and painted flat on sawhorses. Same primer (substrate-driven) and finish (QT-driven) as carcass. Flat orientation allows gravity-assisted leveling.

risk_notes.topic: MDF fiber swelling on cut edges
risk_notes.risk: Irreversible fiber swelling if water-based product contacts raw MDF cut/routed edges — built-in carcass has extensive cut edges at shelf dado joints, face frame rabbets, and routed profiles
risk_notes.mitigation: Always seal MDF edges with shellac/oil-based sealer (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC) before any latex product. Built-in openings have high edge density — multiple shelves, dividers, and back panel rabbets per opening.

risk_notes.risk: Doors closed before waterborne alkyd fully cured (< 5-7 days) — paint surfaces bond together permanently
risk_notes.mitigation: Minimum 5-7 day cure before closing doors per FFD SS15.11.3. Keep doors propped open during cure. Drawer fronts reinstalled but left slightly open. Plan painting schedule to allow cure time before final close-out.

risk_notes.risk: Resin and green mineral streaks bleed through non-stain-blocking primer on bare FJP built-in components
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK. Stain-blocking is MANDATORY for bare FJP. NOT optional.

risk_notes.topic: Brush marks on flat built-in surfaces
risk_notes.risk: Visible brush marks on shelf faces and door fronts from overworking waterborne product — flat horizontal surfaces show marks clearly
risk_notes.mitigation: Waterborne philosophy (FFD SS15.3.1): Apply, tip once, walk away. 2-minute window for waterborne products. Rigid-block sanding between coats (FFD SS15.4.1). Door fronts painted flat for gravity-assisted leveling. Build finish through multiple sanded coats.

risk_notes.risk: Over-application on vertical surfaces inside deep openings leads to runs and drips — enclosed compartments retain fumes and moisture longer
risk_notes.mitigation: Light coats, proper technique, good lighting inside compartments. DEEP and VERY_DEEP modifiers account for slower pace. Check vertical surfaces (sides, back panel, shelf undersides) for runs before each coat dries.

risk_notes.topic: Poor primer adhesion on factory-primed surface
risk_notes.risk: Factory primer too thin, contaminated, or damaged during construction handling
risk_notes.mitigation: Inspect factory primer during prep. If damaged or suspect, treat as SS_BARE (full prime). Standard scuff sand provides adhesion for intact primer.

risk_notes.risk: Hinges and hardware not returned to exact original locations after painting — doors hang crooked or don't close properly
risk_notes.mitigation: Label all hardware and hinge locations before removal. Bag and tag hardware by opening number. Clean paint from screw holes before reinstallation. Account for paint film thickness on hinge mortises.

risk_notes.risk: Deep compartments with restricted airflow extend dry and cure times beyond manufacturer PDS — risk of premature recoat causing solvent entrapment or finish failure
risk_notes.mitigation: Allow extra dry time for deep compartments. Prop all doors/drawers open during cure. Use fans for air circulation in enclosed rooms. Temperature and humidity monitoring — cold or humid conditions compound the effect.

material_notes.dual_system_architecture: TWO independent material system layers: (1) Primer systems are substrate-driven with 5 distinct paths (MDF edge seal, MDF face prime, FJP stain-block, hardwood tannin-block, softwood standard). (2) Finish systems are QT-driven (SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, SYS_FF_PREMIUM). Any primer can pair with any finish. Identical architecture to SF_WOOD_WALL_NC, SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC, SF_ARCH_ELEMENT_NC.
material_notes.mdf_two_step_note: MDF requires two-step prime: edge seal with shellac/oil-based (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC), then face prime with latex (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX). Order is mandatory. Built-in MDF carcass has extensive cut edges — shelf dado joints, face frame rabbets, routed profiles, divider joints.
material_notes.opening_count_coverage_model: Coverage is EA-based per opening tier using SF-equivalent conversion for material quantity planning: S~2SF, M~5SF, L~10SF, XL~20SF per BuiltIns Quantification System v2.0. These are material planning estimates only — production rates use EA/hr directly. Deep openings have more interior surface area and consume proportionally more material.
material_notes.door_material_note: Door/drawer fronts use same material systems as carcass. Estimated ~6 SF per door/drawer front (face + edges). Painted flat on sawhorses — gravity-assisted leveling. 5-7 day cure for waterborne alkyd (QT4+) before closing doors.
material_notes.product_classification: Advance is waterborne alkyd. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel (RC-006).
material_notes.elevated_spackle_note: Built-ins have high fastener density — shelves, dividers, face frames, and back panels all fastened. NC fastener fill uses overfill-sand-flush method with HIGH waste factor per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine. 3-5x standard spackle consumption per Millwork Doctrine.
material_notes.enclosed_compartment_note: Built-in compartments are enclosed spaces that retain humidity and fumes longer than open surfaces. Extended dry times, increased overspray waste inside compartments (spray), and trapped sanding dust are all built-in-specific material and technique considerations.
material_notes.hardware_handling: All hardware (hinges, knobs, pulls, catches) removed before coating and reinstalled after cure. Hardware removal/reinstall is labor, not material — no material cost. Bag and tag hardware by opening number.

assumptions.value: 350-450 SF/gal for finish coat on primed smooth surface
assumptions.source: Manufacturer PDS data, aligned with trim/window/riser/wainscot/wood wall spec coverage

assumptions.value: S~2SF, M~5SF, L~10SF, XL~20SF per opening tier for material planning
assumptions.note: These are material planning estimates. Actual surface area per opening varies by depth, detail level, and shelf count.

assumptions.source: Research estimate based on typical built-in door dimensions (18-24" wide, 24-36" tall)
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines built-in door SF equivalent. 6 SF is conservative average across typical residential door/drawer sizes.

assumptions.value: 20-30% overspray waste for spray inside enclosed compartments
assumptions.source: Research estimate — higher than open surface spray waste due to enclosed compartment overspray bounce-back
assumptions.note: No doctrine specifies compartment-specific spray waste. 20-30% is conservative — open surface spray waste is typically 10-20%.

assumptions.value: Perimeter + internal joints. Higher than closet shelf due to visible finish quality requirements.
assumptions.source: Research note — 72 LF/tube NC rate per Millwork Doctrine
